background: Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest bank, funded by Italian retail deposits and lending to Italian households and companies, with large wealth management and insurance arms and a smaller international network in Central and Eastern Europe.
synthesis: Ratings are A- on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at BBB+, one on a positive outlook and two on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 25 Nov 2025, grades that sit close to the Italian sovereign's. Capital is mixed against EU and Nordic peers: CET1 of 13.0% is in the bottom quarter, while leverage of 5.7% is above the peer median; liquidity is on the weak side, with LCR of 138% in the bottom quarter and NSFR of 120% below the median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods to 30 Jun 2026. The flagged news is all good: record quarterly earnings on 19 Sep 2026, and earlier a record first half with raised guidance and an upgrade from an agency outside the three.
